reason: The text establishes a theological framework emphasizing divine sovereignty. God explicitly 'hardens Pharaoh's heart' (וַיְחַזֵּ֥ק יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֑ה) repeatedly throughout the narrative, and all the plagues are presented as God's own actions and signs (מוֹפְתִ֥ים). The plagues' purpose is explicitly stated as demonstrating God's power ('that you may know that I am the LORD'). While Pharaoh refuses to release the Hebrew people, the text consistently attributes the causation and control of events to God rather than to human leadership decisions. Moses and Aaron are portrayed as obedient instruments. From the text's theological perspective, ultimate responsibility for the state of the Hebrew people rests with divine will and purpose, not with human leadership choices.
